name: 5-Card Brag
description: 5-Card Brag is a high-powered strategic variation of standard 3-Card Brag. In this version, every player is dealt five cards and must select the best three to form their Brag hand, discarding the other two. This choice phase leads to much higher average hand rankings (Running Flushes and Prials are common) and significantly reduces the luck of the draw. Once hands are set, play proceeds with the classic half-price blind betting and Brag hierarchies.

history.origins: Part of the traditional British multi-card Brag family, 5-Card Brag emerged as a way to provide more strategic depth than the original 3-card game. It shares roots with partition games like Crash and 9-Card Brag.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Multi-card Brag variants gain popularity in British card clubs.
1980s: Becomes a standard Dealer's Choice option in social gambling.
Present: Popular in both physical card rooms and online implementations.
history.cultural: Reflects the British preference for 'choice' based gambling games that allow for more tactical discarding.
history.evolution: The game retains the core vying and blind-betting rules but introduces a pre-play hand optimization phase.

setup.dealing: Every player contributes an ante. Dealer deals five cards face-down to each player. Players choose three to keep and place the other two face-down in a shared muck pile.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.

rules.objective: Win the pot by forming the best three-card hand from the five dealt, or by forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Selection**: Players receive 5 cards and discard 2. 2. **Vying**: Standard Brag betting follows. Players choose to play 'Blind' (without looking at their chosen 3) or 'See'. 3. **Ranks**: Prial > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: The choice of which three cards to keep is the primary skill element.
Blind players bet half the price of Seeing players.
Equal hands favor the player who remained Blind longer.

strategy.basic: With 5 cards to choose from, you should rarely play a hand that isn't at least a Flush. Look for high pairs or consecutive suit sequences.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Hidden' Prial: If you are dealt a pair and two cards of another suit, evaluate if it's better to keep the pair for a safe 'Seeing' bet or gamble on a 'Blind' bet with potentially higher hidden value.
strategy.advanced: Discard Tracking: Since every player mucks two cards, 8-16 cards are taken out of play in a 4-8 player game. Track which ranks are most common in your 5 cards to deduce which suits/ranks are depleted in opponents' hands.
tips: Don't fall in love with a low pair; in 5-card Brag, a low pair is a very weak hand.
If you hold a 3 and two wild cards ('Braggers'), you have the top hand (Prial of 3s).

variations.name: Brag with Braggers
variations.description: Standard variant where J♣, 9♦, and A♦ are wild cards (Braggers).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant uses the same engine structure as the base game; wild cards only affect hand ranking evaluation.

scoring.winCondition: Last player standing or best three-card hand at showdown.

synthesis.shortDescription: A strategic evolution of Brag where more cards mean bigger hands. Deal five, keep three, and enter the classic British vying showdown. With better odds for Prials and Running Flushes, the betting is faster and the bluffs are bolder.
